A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SmartThinker work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SmartThinker benchmark results, multistage training experiments, ablations and distribution analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds 4B out-of-domain evaluations, quantitative reasoning-structure analysis and unimodality tests.

M1.justification: Equation (7) corrects the equal-variance branch to select max(L) when the estimated mu1 < mu2, replacing mu1 > mu2. This changes a limited case of the written procedure. Gaussian estimation, clipping, the one-sided length penalty and the adaptive coefficient remain; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Training and task coverage are retained. MathQA, MMLU, LiveCodeBench and HumanEval already appear in v1 Appendix C.3, and Olympiad distribution tests also pre-exist. The added 4B evaluations and MATH500 reasoning analysis reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same base-model, truncation, ShorterBetter, ThinkPrune-4k and LASER-DE-4096 comparisons. Table 2 retains AutoThink and staged ThinkPrune comparisons, while Figure 7 retains its 1.5B OOD comparators. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the stated 1.5B training budget from 175 to 150 steps, agreeing with the already-reported Table 1; this does not establish a rerun. New supplementary protocols extend OOD evaluation to Qwen3-4B and classify reasoning on 50 randomly selected MATH500 problems using DeepSeek-V3.2.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary evidence: Section 4.7 adds systematic reasoning-structure analysis beyond the retained single example, Appendix C.1 examines unimodality among distributions failing Gaussian testing, and Section 4.5 extends OOD robustness evaluation to 4B. These address mechanism, distributional assumptions and transfer across models.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 adds Hartigan’s dip test for distributions failing the Kolmogorov–Smirnov test, introducing a new statistical testing procedure. Existing Gaussian tests and four responses per benchmark question remain. No new independent-run counts, seeds or performance confidence intervals are reported.

E6.justification: New result sets cover 4B OOD performance, reasoning-category shares and unimodality (Tables 3, 5 and 8). Pivotal reasoning is reported as 6.13% for the base model versus 16.04% for SmartThinker. Table 2 revises AutoThink-Stage2 average accuracy from 62.3 to 62.6 and ThinkPrune-4k→SmartThinker AMC23 length from 5134 to 3939; the ablation table changes SmartThinker MATH500 length from 2654 to 2645. Table 1 is unchanged. Appendix C.3 also changes the accuracy-preservation exception from ShorterBetter to SmartThinker, contradicting the retained figure and new table.

T1.justification: The equal-variance inequality corrections in Equations (5) and (7) resolve disagreement with the existing Appendix A.2 derivation. Equation (4) replaces the formulation involving step-level semantic density with a per-trajectory accuracy/length reward. Appendix A.3 corrects the KL target from the old policy to the reference policy. The central Gaussian theorem and proof remain.

C1.justification: The two central contributions remain. The headline compression claim changes from 52.5% average compression in the abstract, and 52.2% in the introduction, to 52.6% compression without the average qualifier. The 16.6% AIME25 accuracy gain is explicitly identified as relative, refining the quantitative claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that OOD gains reflect beneficial reasoning paths rather than additional mathematical training, and that sparse outcome rewards improve reasoning structure. Appendix C.1 additionally argues that mostly unimodal non-Gaussian distributions remain usefully described by means and variances. The original limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses training-data provenance for reused baseline models and identifies DeepSeek-V3.2 and the ShorterBetter prompt source for the new judge analysis. It also corrects the documented 1.5B training-step count. The training framework, other principal hyperparameters, original task prompt and code-access link remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds BubbleSpec and removes O1-Pruner from the references, correcting the OpenAI o1 attribution to the already-cited system card. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for the same works. SmartThinker’s positioning around dynamic length calibration remains.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites polish the abstract, introduction, method explanations and conclusion, with terminology and subsection-title corrections. v2 adds OOD and reasoning-structure subsections, acknowledgements and another correspondence contact, while retaining the overall narrative organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3, 5 and 8; Table 3 redisplays existing 1.5B OOD results alongside new 4B results. Existing figures are retained, with caption corrections and page reflow. Older tables are renumbered or relocated rather than replaced by substantially redesigned displays.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves several equation and reporting inconsistencies and adds useful generalization, reasoning-structure and distribution diagnostics. These incrementally strengthen the retained study. Benefits are tempered by the erroneous 'except SmartThinker' statement in Appendix C.3 and Section 4.5’s causal attribution, which exceeds what the OOD comparisons establish.
